description: DG-6 over-decisiveness — GROUNDED partial resolution: per-battle combat-effectiveness (CEV) friction. Jordan directive 2026-07-22 ('validate emergent results top-down from historical precedent; extend code as required to resolve standing issues using academic research, military theory, mathematics, historical precedent'). Root cause CONFIRMED (mathematical): melee attrition sums N independent per-soldier dice -> CV self-averages ~1/sqrt(N) (measured 0.89->0.06 for N=4->1024); pool scales linearly with troops -> compute_degree near-deterministic from the force ratio -> outcomes collapse to 100%/0% where history shows bands. Fix (two research passes, ~200k tokens; grounding in audit/2026-07-22-mass-battle-stress-test/dg6_friction_resolution.md): keep the self-averaging attrition core, add a per-BATTLE, per-side multiplicative CEV factor M ~ LogNormal(0, sigma^2) drawn ONCE per battle (orchestration._draw_friction_cev, lazy so multi-turn re-entries keep the single draw), multiplying the subunit combat pool (core/exchange). Law of total variance: the attrition term ->0 with N (kept), the once-per-battle shock stays O(1) -> scale-invariant outcome variance (Dupuy CEV / Clausewitz friction / stochastic-Lanchester; Kingman 2002, Beyerchen 1992, Rowland, Sabin Lost Battles). CALIBRATED gauge-INDEPENDENTLY to the Dupuy DLEDB force-ratio win-curve (NOT the gauge, I5): sigma=1.1 reproduces 1.2:1->57% (t55), 1.5:1->62% (t62), 2:1->70% (t70), 3:1->82% (t80). Mechanism verified (test_friction_cev.py, 7): default-inert/byte-exact off; drawn once per battle not per turn; large-force 2:1 collapses to >=95% without friction and stays banded <90% with it (the scale-invariant-variance fix); I1/I2 hold. HONEST FINDING -- friction is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT, ships DEFAULT OFF: the 20-row history gauge moves 6/20 -> 4/20 with uniform friction ON, because (1) envelopment rows (H3/H4) stay ~100% -- their over-decisiveness is STRUCTURAL (envelopment geometry), needing a CONJUNCTIVE gate (Goldsworthy/Sabin: center-holds x cavalry-sufficiency x terrain), not symmetric noise; (2) friction BREAKS the Stage E brace repel (C2/C6 REPELLED->NOT-REPELLED: a big CEV draw lets cavalry break a braced line, but Waterloo-squares repel is near-deterministic) -- friction must be exempted/damped in the brace repel; (3) near-parity rows pushed just out of band. So it ships gated OFF (byte-exact, inert; grid oracle unaffected -- I4). Complete DG-6 resolution = (a) this CEV friction + (b) conjunctive envelopment gate + (c) brace-repel preservation -- scoped as follow-on. needs_jordan: default-flip + the (b)/(c) design calls. No constant tuned to the gauge.

title: d.1 executed: faction Stability sets a strategic unit's morale baseline, superseding PP-711
description: EXECUTION of directive d.1, ruled by Jordan and recorded in ED-MB-0067's second row (2026-09-25) and corrected in its third and fourth rows (2026-09-26): faction state (Stability) sets a unit's starting morale when a battle is built from the strategic layer. Landed at systems/mass_battle/sim/massbattle.py -- _faction_to_unit hardcoded morale=5, morale_start=5 for every faction with its own honest '[canonical: inherited default -- see GAP above]' comment; PP-711 (.designs/systems/mass_battle/reference/mass_battle_v30.md:230-231,:660, General's Command + unit quality modifier) was ratified prose no code ever implemented, so this is a NEW derivation, not an edit to prior logic. Added _morale_start_from_stability: sta = getattr(faction, 'Sta', _GarrisonStub.Sta); return max(1, min(7, round(sta))). THE FLOOR-AND-ROUND MAPPING IS THIS IMPLEMENTATION'S OWN CHOICE, JORDAN-VETOABLE, NOT PART OF THE d.1 RULING ITSELF: Sta and Morale share a 0-7 registry-declared ladder (descriptors.faction_bounds('Sta') = (0, 7), confirmed by test_faction_stat_bounds.py), so identity-plus-round is the natural map, but the floor is set at 1 rather than 0 because canon's Morale floor is 1 while the general is present (mass_battle_v30.md:254 -- 'While general is present: Morale floor = 1. At Morale 0: unit routs.') and rout fires at morale<=0 (core/state.py:189, hierarchy/units.py:2454-2455) -- a Stability-0 faction must not field a pre-routed unit. The concept synthesis's own Stability -> s0 mapping (proposals/2026-09-25-squad-engagement-synthesis.md) is itself an open placeholder at the faction scale, so this precision was not already ruled. _GarrisonStub (the uncontrolled-territory defender, no backing Faction) is held at the PRE-change flat morale-start of 5 so the swap is attributable to real factions' Stability alone -- verified by a dedicated regression test (test_garrison_stub_keeps_the_pre_change_morale_of_five). GOLDENS REGENERATED, and why: engine/tests/test_mc_v18_regression.py (seed-0, n=2: win_share {Church 50 -> 0, Hafenmark 50 -> 0, Varfell 0 -> 100}, battles_mean 36.0 -> 37.0) and engine/tests/test_f7_smoke_oracle.py (seed-42, n=8: win_share Crown 62.5 -> 50.0 among other moves, scenes_resolved 407 -> 516, and the Hafenmark-elimination-lockout mechanism trace re-pointed from seed 44 -- no longer eliminates anyone under this change -- to seed 47, verified to isolate the same one-faction-permanently-zeroed shape) -- both move because _try_conquest -> resolve_mass_battle -> _faction_to_unit runs on every campaign-reachable Military Conquest, so every seeded battle now starts at a Stability-derived morale instead of a flat 5. CONTROLS held byte-exact, before and after: tests/valoria/test_mass_battle_byte_exact.py, tests/valoria/test_field_golden_pins.py, and tools/ci_golden_modes_check.py's three pinned modes (unit_field_mor0, cell_field_mor0, cell_legacy_mor1) -- none of them route through _faction_to_unit, which is what isolates this change to the strategic seam alone. PP-711's supersession is filed as its own row in registers/supersession_register.yaml, per CLAUDE.md 0.05 (the .md itself is reference only and is not the fix).

description: CORRECTION to this id's rows 3-4, caught by an adversarial code review (Opus, 2026-09-26) of the d.1 implementation those rows described, and independently verified by the orchestrating session before this row was written. Every prior row on this id, and the original Fable audit that started this thread, cited 'PP-711' for the morale STARTING formula ('general's Command + unit quality modifier'). That is wrong. PP-711 (= MB-03, per registers/patch_register_active.yaml's 2026-05-02 renumbering note) is the BATTLE-BOUNDARY RESET rule -- '.designs/systems/mass_battle/reference/mass_battle_v30.md:660' headed 'Morale reset between battles (PP-711, MB-03)' -- and it is implemented and LIVE: systems/mass_battle/sim/orchestration.py's reset_morale_between_battles cites '[canonical: ... params/mass_combat.md §PP-711 (Morale resets between battles)]' in its own docstring and is called at every campaign battle boundary. The starting-FORMULA sentence ('Starting = general's Command + unit quality modifier (cap 7)', mass_battle_v30.md:230-231) carries NO PP tag of its own -- it was never ratified as its own patch, only ever described in prose, and mass_battle_v30.md:660 merely references it for context. THAT untagged sentence is what d.1 actually supersedes; PP-711 itself stands. Every surface citing 'supersedes PP-711' or 'PP-711 ... overwritten' needs this correction: registers/supersession_register.yaml's PP-711 entry, ED-MB-0068's ledger row (uncommitted at time of writing -- corrected directly there, not by a further row, since it never shipped in its wrong form), massbattle.py's docstrings/comments, the new test file's docstring, and both re-recorded golden blocks in engine/tests/. This repository's own citation-verification discipline (CLAUDE.md §0.1 pt 3: 'a citation you have not opened is not a citation') was violated three times in a row on this exact fact before this row caught it -- worth naming plainly rather than quietly fixing.

Round-1 build shipped a crash on the legacy-lattice arm (MB_NODE_COHESION=0) and a naive suspend-on-yield/retreat priority rule. Round-2 Opus review found the crash-fix silently swapped one bug for another (a route-only atom marched full-speed forever instead of holding position, F5); that 'suspend' was itself wrong, since yield_active can flip false because discipline DEGRADES further, not because the pressure eased, and stance=='retreat' has no engine writer at all (F3 -- reversed to abandon-on-detection, not suspend-and-resume); that an unreachable waypoint had no progress bound at all, independent of yield/retreat (F2 -- a tick-bounded stall-breaker was added, same shape as ENVELOP_ORBIT_CAP's force-commit); that the documented resume-from-index escape hatch computed the wrong budget (F6 -- fixed by threading an explicit start_idx through both the clamp and the cursor assignment); and two eager-validation gaps (F11 -- a bare-tuple route waypoint and a non-string fire_signal name now raise at Order construction, not mid-battle).

A2 (perception-limited order conditions): core/contact.py's _visible_enemy_cells filters the enemy_range: order trigger through a facing cone (FOV_HALF_DEG, composed on the existing MB_FACING_MODEL/MB_FACING_FOV_GATE flags after a round-2 fix -- round 1 ran unconditionally). A round-1 standalone MB_SIGHT_RANGE distance constant was removed as provably dead by construction (every enemy_range:/refuse_range value in the package is <=10, and the constant had to be set above that to avoid regressing the one shipped consumer). A false docstring claim that FOV_HALF_DEG's 105 deg matched the GREEN/YELLOW boundary (actually 90 deg) was corrected.

A4 (go-codes): a sixth Order trigger kind, signal:NAME, fires once NAME is in the issuing Unit's new fired_signals set; an order's behavior may set the pseudo-field fire_signal:NAME as the real, order-writable path to release it (round-1 shipped the trigger kind with no way to actually fire one in a battle; round-2 closed that). fired_signals is cleared at reset_morale_between_battles, matching the ED-MB-0022 feigned/overextended precedent.

A6 (missile ammunition and resupply): Subunit.eff_volleys/drain_volleys/resupply_volleys, mirroring stamina's own per-subunit, own-else-inherited-Unit ledger exactly. Round 1 put this on percell._ColBlock (column-block granularity); round 2 found that structurally unsound (a column position is shared across whatever subunits currently occupy it, so ammo could regenerate for free under MB_CLOSE_RANKS=1 or silently stop being metered under MB_CLOSE_RANKS=0) and moved it to the Subunit/Unit ledger instead. Round 1 also shipped MB_AMMO_ENABLED defaulting OFF, reasoning neither producer nor orchestrator sandbox could produce a CI-reference-accurate bat.py digest here -- THAT PREMISE WAS WRONG: it was measured with a hand-rolled bat.py invocation setting only ~4 of the ~40 env vars tools/ci_golden_modes_check.py's FIELD_PINS actually pins (missing MB_FACING_MODEL among others), so it silently tested an unpinned, different configuration. Properly pinned (the real tool), this sandbox reproduces the committed golden byte-for-byte for all three modes the tool covers (unit_field_mor0, cell_field_mor0, cell_legacy_mor1). Round 3 reversed the default back to ON, re-recorded cell_legacy_mor1's digest in bat.py (the only one of the three that actually moves -- both field modes are confirmed digest-identical on/off because their battery archer locks into melee contact after one approach and never re-enters volley range), and reclassified the three ammo constants from _KNOWN_INERT into FIELD_PINS. Round 2 also found the ammo mechanism's own per-subunit claim was false the moment it was used through the actual production army builder: engine.build_army's per-subunit kwarg-forwarding tuple omitted 'volleys' entirely, so every ranged subunit built through the public army constructor silently shared ONE pool with its melee siblings -- the same column-sharing bug, relocated one level up (F4, HIGH; fixed in build_army and the gauge harness's make_mixed_unit, mirroring DG-4's own per-subunit morale-seeding precedent). And that a ranged kiter out of ammo would hold its wide standoff band forever, contributing nothing, since _kite_goal's far bound keyed on unit_type=='ranged' alone (F7; now also requires eff_volleys > 0, falling back to the melee reach bound once empty).

DISCLOSED, NOT FIXED (out of scope for this batch): unit_legacy_mor0/cell_legacy_mor0 mismatch bat.py's committed EXPECTED even properly pinned -- confirmed, by a clean-tree/modified-tree digest comparison, to be a PRE-EXISTING drift this batch did not cause. The likely mechanism: tests/valoria/test_mass_battle_byte_exact.py's own BAT_PY constant still points at tests/sim/mass_battle/bat.py, which no longer exists (the file lives at systems/mass_battle/sim/bat.py) -- the same component-form repoint-sweep miss tools/ci_golden_modes_check.py's own docstring already documents surviving once elsewhere. That test currently passes/skips/xfails cleanly (does not silently report a false green), so this is a stale-path bug to fix in its own right, not an emergency. Separately, this session found and corrected a THIRD citation error of its own, in massbattle.py's d.1 docstring (ED-MB-0068): the claim that reset_morale_between_battles is 'called at every campaign battle boundary' has no confirmed production call site (grep-verified against engine/ and this file; only test code calls it directly) -- corrected in place, flagged in HANDOFF_MB.md, not yet resolved which way (a real gap, or PP-711 enforced some other way -- fresh Unit construction per battle rather than a reset).

A8 (ROUT_CASCADE_FRAC sweep) and every Tier-2 item (A3+C5 officers/span-of-control, A7 terrain, C2/C3's coupling formula, C4's feigned-retreat mechanics) remain explicitly deferred, per the original planning pass's own assessment that they need a design/slice pass before a coding pass.
